root_cause: The native Escape key listener (_cancelHandler) may fail to call event.preventDefault() due to an early return or exception before the preventDefault statement, allowing the dialog's default close action to occur on the third Escape press.
repair_strategy: Wrap the _cancelHandler logic in a try/finally block to guarantee event.preventDefault() is always executed, preserving the existing conditional behavior.
expected_accessibility_effect: Escape key will no longer dismiss the dialog when keyboard:false, allowing users to press Escape repeatedly without losing focus or closing the dialog, preserving keyboard operability and meeting WCAG 2.1.1 (Keyboard) and 2.4.3 (Focus Order).
functional_risks: The try/finally introduces negligible overhead; no functional change is expected.
When keyboard:true, Escape continues to close the dialog after preventDefault.
Static backdrop transition still occurs when keyboard:false.
Dialog can still be dismissed via the Cancel transfer button or by submitting a valid OTP.
verification_requirements: Press Escape any number of times while the dialog is open with keyboard:false and backdrop:static; the dialog must remain open and focus must stay on the OTP input.
Verify that the static backdrop transition (visual 'bounce') still occurs on Escape presses when keyboard:false.
When keyboard:true, pressing Escape once must close the dialog and move focus back to the trigger button.
Confirm that the Cancel transfer button still sets status to 'Cancelled' and closes the dialog.
Confirm that submitting a valid six‑digit OTP sets status to 'Sent' and closes the dialog.
